newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says Rwanda infiltration death toll 35.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says Rwanda infiltration death toll 35.

text.p: Zaire said on Saturday that infiltrators from Rwanda had killed at least 35 people and wounded three this month during cross-border attacks to destabilise Zaire's eastern refugee zone.

Government spokesman Oscar Lugendo, stepping up a war-of words against the Tutsi-led government in neighbouring Rwanda, told state television everything was being done to ensure the security of Zaireans living in South Kivu province.

The television showed footage of what it said were five Rwandan soldiers captured in Uvira near the border with Burundi. Zaire has accused Burundi, where the Tutsi-led army holds power, and aid groups of helping Rwandan infiltrators.

"From September 10 to 24 armed elements from Rwanda carried out murderous attacks in the zones of Fizi, Baraka and Mwenda... for which the provisional toll it 35 dead and three wounded," Lugendo said.
One of the captured soldiers, speaking halting French, said that they had crossed into Zaire from Burundi.
Human rights groups have accused soldiers of carrying out atrocities in South Kivu against Banyamulenge Tutsis, some of whom have lived in the area for generations.
Zaire is host to over a million Hutus who fled Rwanda in 1994 fearing reprisals after Hutu hardliners killed hundreds of thousands of minority Tutsis and Tutsi rebels seized power.
Relations between Zaire and Rwanda have since deteriorated, with each side accusing the other of sponsoring or failing to stop raids into their territory.
